v.title: Wrexham’s Rising Star Leaves, and Reynolds Gives a Standing Ovation
v.excerpt: Ryan Reynolds salutes Wrexham’s assistant manager Steve Parkin as he exits, after steering the club from non‑league to the Championship.
v.body:
## Quick take
Ryan Reynolds has just applauded Steve Parkin, Wrexham’s assistant manager, who is set to depart after steering the club from the Conference to the Championship. The Hollywood star’s heartfelt tribute underscores how Parkin’s tactical mind has become a blueprint for modern football.

## What happened
Wrexham’s meteoric climb has been nothing short of a fairy‑tale, but the secret sauce has been Steve Parkin’s partnership with manager Rob McElhenney. After a season of battling relegation, Parkin’s innovative set‑piece work and data‑driven approach turned the Dragons into a defensive fortress, earning them a spot in the Championship for the first time in 30 years. Now, with the club’s future plans still murky, Parkin has decided to leave, citing a desire to test himself in a new environment.

Reynolds, who has been a vocal supporter of the club since the Hollywood takeover, took to social media to thank Parkin for “his brilliance, his patience and his belief in the underdog.” The actor’s message resonated across the fanbase, highlighting how the club’s success is a collective effort that extends beyond the marquee names. Parkin’s exit will leave a void that the club must fill quickly if it wants to maintain its momentum.

## Why it matters
- **Tactical Evolution for Barça** – Parkin’s emphasis on high‑press, quick transitions mirrors the philosophy that Guardiola has now adopted at Barcelona. If Barça can learn from Wrexham’s data‑rich approach, it could refine its own build‑from‑back play and regain dominance in La Liga.
- **Player Development Pipeline** – Parkin’s knack for nurturing talent, especially in the midfield, offers a case study for Barcelona’s famed La Masia. Integrating similar analytical tools could accelerate the growth of young prospects like Pedri and Gavi.
- **Seasonal Momentum** – The Dragons’ rise demonstrates how a coherent tactical identity can propel a club from obscurity to the upper echelons of English football. For Barcelona, maintaining such momentum against rivals like Real Madrid and Atlético is crucial to securing a Champions League spot.

## What's next
Watch Wrexham’s next pre‑season fixture against a top Championship side. The club’s new coaching appointment will be revealed in the coming weeks, and the match will be a litmus test for how well the squad adapts to a potentially new tactical philosophy. For Barça fans, any shift in Wrexham’s strategy could signal a new benchmark for tactical innovation across Europe.

*Source: [Reynolds pays tribute as key assistant in Wrexham's rise announces exit](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50603679/wrexham-ryan-reynolds-rob-mcelhenney-assistant-manager)*
